findings.title: a `None` evidence for a window is silently accepted
findings.difference: original: `isinstance(evidence, str)` is false for `None`, so `assess_lifecycle(None, ...)` raises, the run catches it, emits `lifecycle.monitor_unavailable` and names the signal under `unavailable`; candidate: `evidence is not None and not isinstance(evidence, str)` skips the assessment, the window is judged with zero readings, nothing is inserted, nothing is emitted, nothing is reported unavailable
findings.input_class: an evidence callable that returns `None` for a window (outside the declared `MonitorEvidence | str`)
findings.production_reachability: not reachable as typed: production evidence comes from `LiveEvidence.for_window`, which returns a `MonitorEvidence` or a not-run string; only a caller violating the `Evidence` type produces `None`

findings.killing_test: a runner over scripted sources whose evidence callable returns `None` for one due window; assert the summary names the signal under `unavailable`, `windows_evaluated` is 0 and exactly one `lifecycle.monitor_unavailable` record is emitted

findings.title: the purpose-bound writers accept extra arguments and can be redirected
findings.difference: original: `admit`, `flag` and `retire` are closures of exactly five parameters, a sixth positional or an unknown keyword raises `TypeError`; candidate: lambdas with defaults `_t` (target) and `_a` (authority), so a sixth positional argument or `_t=` rebinds the target and the request reaches the store
findings.input_class: a call of a bound writer with a sixth or seventh positional argument, or with `_t` or `_a` as keywords (outside the typed `LifecycleWriters` signatures)
findings.production_reachability: not reachable through the typed call sites the review read (every production caller passes five arguments under mypy strict); the domain's `refusal_reason` still gates a mismatched target at the store
findings.nearest_test: tests/unit/test_lifecycle_store_db.py::TestTheTableOnTheDatabase::test_the_retirement_command_binds_only_the_human_route (the route per writer, with five arguments)
findings.killing_test: call `bind_writers(store).retire(signal, version, evidence, revision, reason, LifecycleState.ADMITTED, "census")` and assert `TypeError`; likewise `admit(..., _t=LifecycleState.RETIRED)`

findings.title: partial CLI output on a stored-row fault is lost
findings.probes: P03, P04, P18; 6.5 `compare` pair corpus 24/300 and solver counterexample
findings.difference: original echoes each reproduced line as it is computed, so the lines before a malformed stored row are printed and then `KeyError` ends the command; candidate collects the lines and echoes after the loop, so nothing is printed before the same `KeyError` and exit 1
findings.input_class: a stored reading row lacking `disposition`, `value` or `monitor` after one or more well-formed rows (inside `_compare`'s declared `Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]`)
findings.production_reachability: not reachable through the store's own writes: `LifecycleStore.readings` returns rows `MonitorRunner._append` wrote with every column; it needs a corrupted or hand-edited `signal_monitor_reading` row
findings.killing_test: `lifecycle readings` with the store's `readings()` patched to return a well-formed row followed by a row without `value`; assert the first monitor's line is in the output before the command fails with `KeyError`

findings.title: exception metadata of refusals differs
findings.difference: candidate raises every `TransitionRefused` with `from None` (`__suppress_context__` True; on the write-clash path `__context__` is None where the original keeps the `IntegrityError`); messages, types, written rows, refused rows, clock reads and receipts agree
findings.input_class: any refusal (stale revision, domain refusal, write clash), observed through `__context__` and `__suppress_context__` only
findings.production_reachability: reachable on every refusal, but only tracebacks and logging see it; no caller the review read inspects the chain
findings.killing_test: after a write clash, catch `TransitionRefused` and assert `__context__` is the `IntegrityError` and `__suppress_context__` is False, if the chain is part of the contract; otherwise record F4 as accepted traceback-only drift

findings.production_reachability: not reachable in production: nothing patches these names at run time; the seed tests and the oracle patch around the whole run, where both trees agree

findings.title: error ordering under double malformation in the projection
findings.probes: 6.5 `standing` pair: corpus 2/300 and the solver counterexample, replayed on both trees (`e5-standing-replay-2`); not among the 128 probes of 6.3
findings.difference: with `standing = None` and a baseline whose `states` holds a non-mapping, the original reads `standing.signal` first (`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'signal'`), the candidate builds the baseline view first (`AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'`); same type, different message
